title: Review action
responsibility: Perform review-status changes from the application through the existing typed write path — lock, fresh read inside the lock, atomic write — reusing `lib/tools/review-status.mjs` rather than reimplementing it, and reaching it through the server adapter layer.
notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ IT IS THE FIRST LOCKING CAPABILITY THE ADAPTER MUST EXPOSE, and DEC-0021 holds locking modules back for individual review precisely so this one is examined rather than arriving as a line in an adapter. A Server Component may run concurrently in ways a CLI never does. ⚠️ `reviewStatus` ONLY. #82's two-axis split is doing work here: review progress is the application's to change and `lifecycle` is not, and a single `status` field would have let this endpoint retire an artifact by accident. ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it does not decide whether a status change is allowed — the typed tool owns that, and one implementation serves both the CLI and the app (#47). ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-29 BY TSK-0012 (EVD-0072), after the individual review DEC-0021 requires. ACC-0034 passes. ⚠️ IT REUSES `lib/tools/review-status.mjs` RATHER THAN REIMPLEMENTING IT, which is the whole of why this could be approved: the lock, the fresh read inside the lock and the atomic write are the ones the CLI already used, so there is no second copy to drift. ⚠️ THE ADAPTER EXPOSES ONE WRITE AND ADMITS ONE CALLER. `app/server/review.js` re-exports `setReviewStatus` and nothing else that writes, and `shellBoundaryConfig` names the Server Action as its only permitted consumer. Both are pinned by tests that fail by name when a second write or a second caller appears — a second caller being a second place the content lock can be taken from, which is the review needing to happen again. ⚠️ THE HARD PART IS IN A MODULE WITH NO `server-only`, for the reason CMP-0017's client half is: everything decidable about a write — refusals before the lock is taken, a bad status never reaching disk, what two concurrent submissions leave behind — is reachable only from plain Node, and concurrency is what a browser test is worst at provoking on purpose.
